display.title: The Sukkah: Surrounded by a Mitzvah from Head to Toe
display.summary_short: Why the sukkah is unlike any other mitzvah: it surrounds us completely with a holy 'shadow of faith', and the Ushpizin come to visit. A real smile makes it beautiful.
display.summary_long: A Sukkos talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given between Yom Kippur and Sukkos. Uncle Yossi explains that after Yom Kippur has wiped our record clean, we show our joy by starting a new mitzvah right away, as the Shulchan Aruch teaches: building the sukkah. Most mitzvos use one part of the body, but the sukkah surrounds all of us from head to toe, along with our clothes, tables and dishes. The Zohar calls its holiness 'Tzila d'Meheimnusa', the shadow of faith, which strengthens our belief in Hashem who feeds and shelters us. Each night the Ushpizin visit: Avraham, Yitzchak, Yaakov, Yosef, Moshe, Aharon and Dovid HaMelech, with one of them as the main guest each night. So we behave our best in the sukkah, and the easiest decoration is a real smile, which is contagious. Children are encouraged to invite a friend or relative who has no sukkah of their own.
display.lesson: The sukkah wraps us in faith in Hashem; enter it with a real smile and share it with someone who has no sukkah.

date.note: Clip of episode 398 ('a few days before Sukkos', after Yom Kippur 5750). The same talk also aired in episode 447.
